locators: Results, paragraphs on hit rate, false alarm rate, d-prime, and response time
source_routes.prior_source_status: unresolved occurrence, not selected empirical report

findings.test: t(110)=3.32; p=.001 for combined audio vs control; earcon vs speech p=.749
Welch ANOVA F(2,65.60)=5.97; p=.004; no earcon-vs-speech difference p=.439

cautions: The earcon differed from speech in content, spectral distribution and potential perceived urgency: no isolated 'tone versus voice' causal mechanism.
The non-significant d-prime result does not demonstrate equivalence or absence of an effect.
Human email classifications and intentionally fallible auditory advice are different from objective hazard detection. Do not treat hit-rate preference as unequivocal safety improvement.
Sample identity, eligibility, PDFs, figure data and correction status await R006/R009; visual acuity/hearing and student sample limit transfer.

source_routes.title: Warning users about cyber threats through sounds
source_routes.access_extent: publisher open-access article rendered text, Abstract, §§3.1–3.2, §4.2, §§5.1–5.3 and conclusion; tables/figures referenced by HTML but source images and PDF not inspected
locators: §5.2 Results for the In Context study

abstract_percentages.in_context_correct_threat_identification: about 73% (abstract); §5.2 says scenario values from 73% to 100%

findings: Three security threat families: phishing, malware download and form filling.
In-context evaluation used real websites with simulated/safe warning scenarios, not live malicious attacks.
Section 5.3.1 records participants' proposed actions, not observed real-world prevented attacks.
Current sighted study is explicitly without distractors; comparison with an earlier visually impaired group does not establish matched experimental controls.

cautions: No primary source-file hash or figure/table visual verification.
The 26 and previous 5 are not declared two independent studies/samples here; R006 must resolve publication/participant relationships.
Study compares recognition, attention and stated intended action, not validated threat-detection correctness or longitudinal retention.
Do not interpret 'all heard alerts' as accurate meaning comprehension or completed protective action.
